label: D1 after unrewarded S1 visit, scaled by preceding losing streak
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == -9) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == -1)
explanation: Active only at D1 (GO/D2 are ~0). Magnitude is set by the last trial being an unrewarded visit to S1 and by how long the losing streak is. A single a1 S1 u after a rewarded trial gives a modest activation (~0.3); a2 S1 u (rare, unrewarded) alone gives about zero (weight -0.79 cancels the base). Each extra unrewarded trial before it adds a lot (+0.74 if trial -2 unrewarded, a further +0.70 if trial -3 also unrewarded), so a run of losses ending in S1 drives it to ~3, whichever action was chosen. Lower ideal-observer belief that S1 is good raises it a little (belief_lo weight -0.15). D1 after S2 unrewarded or after any reward stays at 0. Leftover error: window-start trials whose history is outside the window (some reach ~3 but get predicted ~0.2); belief does not stand in for the missing streak. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.56, against an all-cues ceiling of 0.47 and 0.37 for all observed cues. The last-trial pattern alone gives 0.25 (dev). Uses only observed quantities, so there is no measurable loss from dropping value/policy (the policy decile reference was only 0.04).

issues: Magnitudes are overstated. A long losing streak ending in an S1 loss gives a mean of about 1.9 to 2.0 above baseline when the last choice was a1, and 1.25 to 1.66 when it was a2 (cell fits B*(prev_action)*(r-2==0)*(r-3==0)[*(r-4==0)]). About 3 is the peak seen in the examples, not the typical value.

'Whichever action was chosen' is only roughly true. After an S1 loss preceded by one loss, a1 gives +1.40 and a2 gives +0.70. With 3 or more losses the two get closer (1.97 vs 1.66) but a2 stays lower.
'One a1 S1 u after a rewarded trial gives about 0.3' is too high. The fitted cell is about +0.10 over baseline. The claim that a2 S1 u alone gives about zero holds (cell about +0.07).

The 'losing streak' is losses in any state: an earlier loss in S2 counts about the same (extra weight -0.055 for S2). What carries a little extra signal is whether the agent chose a1 on trial -2 (+0.47, dev +0.016). The magnitude also grows later in the episode, beyond the additive timing baseline (B*ep_trial/100 weight +0.40, dev +0.02). Neither is mentioned, but both effects are small.

The prev_action==2 weight of -0.79 depends on belief_lo being in the model (without it the weight is -0.25), because a2 choices go with low belief_lo. The 'cancels the base' story is a reading of collinear weights, not a clean effect of the action.

The worst misses are D1 steps at the start of a window where the earlier trials fall outside the window: actual about 3, predicted about 0.2 to 0.8. This matches the explanation's own caveat and is a limit of the data, not a fixable error class. misses otherwise shows only a uniform intercept offset of -0.05 at D1, and GO and D2 are about zero.
Test R^2 beyond timing reproduces at 0.564. My best 8-term set (adding the trial -2 a1 choice and episode-time interactions) reaches 0.577 on test, so no large systematic gap remains.
